title: Explain the Purpose of Cloud-Native Design Concepts

sections.title: What You Are Learning
paragraphs: A cloud-native application is designed to take advantage of capabilities provided by cloud environments instead of simply treating the cloud like somebody else's server room.
CompTIA wants you to understand several design ideas that help cloud applications become easier to scale, maintain, connect, and change.

sections.title: Maestro Focus
paragraphs: Is this design trying to reduce infrastructure management, separate application components, distribute work, or help services find one another?
sections.callout: Independent services + managed cloud capabilities + dynamic communication → think cloud-native design.

sections.title: Cloud-Provided Managed Services
paragraphs: A managed service allows the cloud provider to operate more of the underlying technology for the customer.
Instead of building, patching, and maintaining every supporting system yourself, you consume the capability as a service.
Think: Use the cloud provider's managed tool instead of building everything from scratch.
The major benefit is reducing operational work so the organization can concentrate on its application or business function.
sections.callout: If the company wants to reduce administration of underlying infrastructure → think cloud-provided managed service.

sections.title: Microservices
paragraphs: A microservices architecture divides an application into smaller services that perform individual functions.
Instead of one enormous application where everything is tightly connected, separate services can handle different jobs.
User authentication, product inventory, payment processing, and notifications could each operate as separate services.
Think: One big application becomes a team of smaller specialists.
A change to one microservice may be possible without rebuilding the entire application.
sections.callout: If an application is divided into small independently operating services → think microservices.

sections.title: Loosely Coupled Architecture
paragraphs: A loosely coupled architecture keeps components from depending too heavily on one another.
One component can change or fail without automatically forcing every other component to fail.
Think: Connected, but not chained together.
This improves flexibility because components can be modified more independently.
sections.callout: If components need independence so changes or failures do not cascade through the entire application → think loosely coupled architecture.

sections.title: Fan-Out
paragraphs: Fan-out describes sending one event, message, or piece of work to multiple destinations or consumers.
Imagine one notification arriving and then being distributed to several different services.
Think: One comes in → many go out.

entries.title: Order Processing Example
paragraphs: A customer places an order. That single event could trigger inventory processing, billing, shipping, and customer notification.
entries.recognitionCue: If one event must trigger multiple independent actions → think fan-out.

sections.title: Service Discovery
paragraphs: In a dynamic cloud environment, services may appear, disappear, move, or scale.
Service discovery allows services to locate other services they need to communicate with without relying entirely on fixed locations.
Think: Instead of memorizing everyone's address, ask where the service currently lives.
sections.callout: If dynamically changing services need to find one another → think service discovery.

sections.title: Recognition Cues
bullets: Provider handles supporting platform or service → Managed service
Application divided into smaller independent functions → Microservices
Components should not strongly depend on each other → Loosely coupled architecture
One event goes to several consumers → Fan-out
Services dynamically locate other services → Service discovery

entries.title: Microservices vs. Loosely Coupled Architecture
paragraphs: They often work together, but they are not identical.
Microservices describes breaking an application into smaller services. Loose coupling describes reducing dependencies between components.
A system can contain multiple components without those components being properly loosely coupled.

entries.title: Fan-Out vs. Service Discovery
paragraphs: Fan-out means distributing work. Service discovery means finding services.
One message needing five consumers points to fan-out. A service needing to locate another changing service points to service discovery.

sections.title: Maestro Recognition Sheet
bullets: Provider handles underlying service operations → Managed service
Large application broken into small services → Microservices
Components operate with minimal dependency → Loosely coupled architecture
One event triggers many destinations → Fan-out
Dynamic services need to find each other → Service discovery
